title: Collision avoidance coordination among mega-constellations
bottleneck: With Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper, and others operating tens of thousands of satellites, conjunctions are routine — but there is no common traffic protocol: operators use different ephemeris formats, maneuver thresholds, and communication channels, and automated avoidance systems must negotiate right-of-way in seconds without a shared standard. A miscoordinated maneuver can turn a near-miss into a collision, and the maneuver burden in fuel and service interruption grows with constellation size.
why_it_blocks: Mega-constellations are the dominant new debris-source risk; without coordination standards, the busiest orbital shells become a game of chicken played by algorithms that cannot talk to each other.
current_state: Operators share data via Space-Track and commercial providers; automated conjunction assessment is standard at SpaceX. No binding international space traffic coordination protocol exists.
